<case_prompt>
A 38-year-old female presents to the physician at a medical center in an endemic tropical country 2 days after receiving a viral vector COVID-19 vaccine. She reports the acute onset of myalgia, high fever, and a widespread skin rash.

On physical examination, vital signs reveal a body temperature of 38.5 °C, blood pressure of 120/80 mmHg, pulse rate of 85 beats per minute, and respiratory rate of 16 breaths per minute. A cutaneous rash is observed across the skin. Initial diagnostic laboratory workup demonstrates an isolated decreased platelet count of 80 x 10^3/microL. A baseline coagulation profile is completely normal without abnormalities.
</case_prompt>

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered because the acute onset of fever, myalgia, rash, and thrombocytopenia coincided temporally with vaccination 2 days prior; however, the coagulation profile showed no abnormalities or consumptive coagulopathy, and the patient resided in a tropical region with high endemicity for vector-borne infections.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: This case was firstly suspicious for a possible vaccine adverse reaction. Nevertheless, there is no coagulation profile abnormality.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered because viral hemorrhagic fevers are prevalent in this tropical region; targeted viral diagnostics specifically identified the culprit virus rather than other regional hemorrhagic pathogens.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Since the setting is a tropical country that viral hemorrhagic disease is common, further investigation for viral hemorrhagic disease was performed.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: The pivotal diagnostic turning point was laboratory confirmation of acute arboviral infection via non-structural protein 1 antigen detection (NS1Ag positive), confirming acute disease.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Further laboratory tests confirm that there is a positive result of dengue virus infection (Dengue NS1Ag + ve). The final diagnosis in this case is dengue.
